First, clear up the name: this is ROB RUN — Kefir's free-to-play crime sandbox on Steam. It is not Roblox, and there is no official mobile, PS5 or Xbox version. Any site selling you a “ROB RUN APK” is not selling Kefir's game — read the hacks warning before you download anything.

01 What ROB RUN actually is

Kefir calls ROB RUN an extraction shooter with a crime empire built on top. Every cop and every criminal in the city is a real player — there are no AI patrols.

You start fresh out of prison in the coastal city of Looty Bay with no cash, no gun and no home, crashing at Lenny's Motel. You rob stores, banks and other players, get the loot out of the city alive, and spend the money on land, a base and businesses out in the desert. Then you climb the Power Pyramid — Hobo → Settlement Resident → Settlement Owner → District Owner → Shadow Governor — before the server wipes after seven days and everyone starts over.

The world has four main areas: Lenny's Motel (safe zone, black market, your first home), Looty Bay (the city — robberies and police), the desert (districts and settlements where bases live), and the prison. Crossing the edge of an area opens the global map, where you pick your next destination.

The whole game in one path

1 · Hobo

Leave prison, base yourself at Lenny's Motel, learn the city as a Civilian.

2 · First cash

Dumpsters and small stores. Sell at a Fence, open a bank account.

3 · Resident

Buy a Land Plot Title, rent a plot, build a house, storage, Workbench, Laundering Desk.

4 · Business owner

Grow Room, lab, cargo — steady money between heists.

5 · The top

Buy a settlement, tax residents, take districts with a clan, fight for Highlands.

03 Your first hour, step by step

Your first hour sets up the whole wipe. Do these in order — most new players lose money by skipping step 6.

  1. Start on the freshest server you can. A new server opens daily in each region (EU 5 PM UTC, East US 8 PM ET). On a fresh server everyone is broke, cops carry pistols only for the first 30 minutes, and plots are still available.
  2. Break out and finish the intro quests. You begin in the district jail with everything confiscated. Talk to the Tattoo Artist first, then use an escape point. The intro quests end at Lenny's Motel — a safe zone (no shooting, no weapons drawn) that works as a black market, a cash stash and a free car rental. Talk to Lenny to unlock the Black Market.
  3. Buy the basic pistol first. Lenny's laptop is the Black Market and your progression board — weapons, gear, housing documents and the police sergeant's badge are all unlocked there first, then bought. The basic pistol costs almost nothing. You can't use it as a Civilian, but the moment the mask goes on you'll want it. Treat it as a consumable: it is not returned when you die.
  4. Grab the free rental car. No active vehicle? Rent one free at any Parking Terminal — and if you lose it, another free one waits at the nearest terminal. Your car matters more than your gun: criminal cars are more manoeuvrable than police cruisers, and the ramps around the city exist to shake a chase.
  5. Scout Looty Bay as a Civilian — before any crime. As a Civilian you lose nothing on death and get treated for free. Drive the city, and note: the bank, the Fence vans (dollar-sign icon), the Sales Center, two exits, where small stores sit, where their alarm panels and cameras are, and where you can park facing your exit. This scouting run is the single highest-value thing a new player can do.
  6. Open a bank account — $5,000. Go to the Central Bank of Looty Bay as a Civilian (no mask) and open an account with the clerk. Without it you cannot launder money, bribe a cop, or join/create a clan. Skipping it is a decision you'll regret the moment real money shows up.
  7. Make your first money: dumpsters, then a small store. Kefir raised dumpster cash at launch — it's free money with zero risk. Then pick a small store near a Fence with no players around, disable its alarm, and rob it (full method in Heists).
  8. Sell at the Fence and pick up your cash. The Fence pays onto the counter, not into your pocket — grab it immediately, because anyone can take it and cops can confiscate it. Fence drop-offs get camped on purpose, so scout the bushes around the van before you drive in.
  9. Stash at Lenny's. Lenny's stash holds up to $150,000 and nothing inside it can be stolen. It's your reserve — everything you carry outside it burns on your first death.
  10. Work toward your plot. Your first big goal is a Land Plot Title and a rented plot (see Base). Spend your first serious money in this order: bank account → replaceable gun and armour → Action Camera → land plot → Cargo Workbench → Grow Room or lab.
Starter gear advice Build around medium armour, a sports bag (more inventory space), spare plates and medical supplies. Wearable gear, armour, bags and recovery items are sold separately from guns — don't blow your whole roll on a rifle and run around in a paper bag.

04 Roles: Civilian, Criminal, Cop

You pick a role every time you enter Looty Bay, and the whole party has to pick the same one. Choose before the city chooses for you.

RoleWhat you can doLimits
CivilianExplore and shop safely, free healing, lose nothing on deathCan't use weapons
CriminalPut on a mask and rob; better loot at higher NotorietyEveryone's enemy; loot must be carried out of the city
CopFree gear and a car for the shift; earn from confiscations, arrests and bribesCan only shoot criminals; needs an open slot at the Police Station
  • The mask is the switch. You become a Criminal the moment you put a mask on — and taking it off does not clear the status. You stay a Criminal until you leave Looty Bay.
  • Cops can close the bridges. Leaving the city is how you become a Civilian again — but police can shut the exits, so never assume the way out is open.
  • Solo is a real playstyle, not a handicap. Solo players start at Notoriety 4 with bonuses to loot collection and selling. Parties cap at 3 — Kefir tested bigger groups and found they killed random encounters.

What death actually costs you

SituationEquipped gearBag / loot
Killed while masked (Criminal) in Looty BayLostLost
Surrender / arrested (press Q)KeptTaken
Killed as a Civilian in Looty BayKeptKept
Killed anywhere in the desert / settlementsLostLost

Two more rules worth memorising: dying also wears down your gear's durability (repair is planned, not in yet), and your purchased car survives your death — mods included. The desert has no police, which sounds safe until you notice death there costs you everything, every time.

The surrender rule Cornered with good gear on? Surrender (Q). Cops take only your bag and your equipped gear stays on you. Or offer a bribe from your bank account — in $10,000 steps, up to $200,000 — and if the cop accepts, you walk away with everything. Dying is almost always the worst option.

05 Controls & settings

ROB RUN is keyboard-and-mouse only — Steam lists no controller support, and Kefir has not published an official keybind list. Anyone showing you a “complete official controls” chart made it up. What's actually confirmed:

InputActionStatus
QSurrender to policeDocumented in Kefir's guides
HOpen the Shipments menuOfficially documented
EscMenu — your UID is shown under your character name (needed for support and cheat reports)Officially documented
E / hold EContext interactions and lootingCommunity-reported — follow the on-screen prompt
XChange camera shoulderCommunity-reported default
ZHolster weaponCommunity-reported default

Everything can be rebound in Settings — do it before your first robbery, and double-check the inventory actions (quick transfer, take all, split stack, drop, destroy). Never experiment with an unfamiliar inventory key while holding a rare item mid-heist.

Watch out Error E-0601 means the game can't detect a keyboard and mouse — it usually appears over Remote Desktop or cloud streaming. Connect a physical keyboard and mouse and play at the PC itself.

06 How to make money — every method, ranked

Money in ROB RUN lives in three states: valuables (need a buyer), dirty cash (can be stolen or confiscated), and laundered bank money (safe from thieves — but not from the wipe). Every method below is about moving up that chain.

MethodWhat it needsSpeedRisk
DumpstersNothing — Kefir raised dumpster cash at launchFastNone unmasked
Small stores → FenceA cheap, replaceable gunFastMedium — your bag is on the line
Action Cameras (charge-up items)Buy $15,000, commit crimes at Notoriety 2+, sell filled for $50,000+PassiveLow
Cargo opened at your WorkbenchA base with a Cargo WorkbenchMediumMedium
ATM eventsA gun and a fast car — pays roughly $150,000–$500,000FastHigh — the whole map sees it
Jewellery stores, Gas Station, hotelsTools: lockpicks, keys, mini drills, USB toolsMediumHigh
Grow Room / Lab productionA plot and the research (see Farm & Lab)SteadyLow–Medium
CollectionsCollection Table at your base; crates up to $500,000 at the top tiersSlowLow
Settlement & clan taxesOwn a settlement / control a districtPassiveMedium — you collect in person
Police workAn open cop slot; confiscations, arrests, bribesSteadyLow — pays less than crime

Where loot gets sold — know your buyers

  • Fence (dollar-sign van in Looty Bay): buys stolen goods for cash, priced off your Notoriety. You must be masked to sell, which is exactly why fences get camped. The cash lands on the counter — pick it up instantly.
  • Smuggler (van) in the covered car parks: buys bulky cargo — crates, safes, suitcases, statues — without opening it. Convenient, but opening cargo yourself at a Workbench pays more since the Nov 5 balance patch.
  • Sales Center in your district: better prices than the city Fence, but only for players renting a plot in that district. One more reason the plot is priority one.

Charge-up items: the quiet money printer

Some Shipments items are worth little empty and a fortune “charged.” Buy them, carry them while you do the matching crimes, then sell the filled version to the Fence — ideally all at once at Notoriety 5 for the +50% bonus.

ItemUnlockBuyHow it fillsSells for
Action Camera I$5,000$15,00040 points of qualifying crimes at Notoriety 2+$50,000
Code Tablet$25,000$20,000Crack 4 safes in Looty Bay$75,000
USB Hacking Tool$50,000$50,000Hack 5 computers in locked rooms$200,000
Legendary Action Camera—$50,000Crimes at Notoriety 4+$200,000–$300,000

Prices are community-tested launch-window figures (checked mid-November 2026). Kefir rebalances often in Early Access — check the in-game laptop before a big buy.

The golden rule of cash

  • Cash in your bag or your car trunk is lost on death and on arrest.
  • Cash sitting at your base can be stolen in a raid.
  • Lenny's stash is protected up to $150,000.
  • Banked, laundered money can't be stolen at all — only the weekly wipe takes it.
  • Never sell a key, a plot document or a blueprint to the Fence. A key sells for about $500; the safe it opens can pay $100,000–$150,000.

07 Notoriety & the Wanted bar

Two bars, opposite meanings. Notoriety is the good one — it makes you money. Wanted is the bad one — it gets you hunted. New players constantly mix them up.

Notoriety builds from crimes committed during a single visit to Looty Bay, and each level raises what the Fence pays you. Sell before you leave the city or the streak — and the bonus — is gone.

Notoriety levelFence bonusWho starts here
Level 2+10%A duo starts at level 2
Level 3+20%—
Level 4+35%Solo players start at level 4
Level 5+50%The cap — sell your charged items here

Higher Notoriety also means better loot rolls and extra valuables more often — but cops press harder the longer your spree runs. The skill is knowing when the next stop risks the whole haul.

The Wanted bar is separate: every civilian you kill adds 1, and at 3 you become Most Wanted — your marker is visible to the whole city. Pull the trigger only when you need to.

Pro move Coming back with a big haul and the Fence looks camped? Leave to the global map, then re-enter Looty Bay as a Civilian and travel to the Fence that way. Even if you're killed, a Civilian keeps both gear and bag.

08 Heists: robbing clean

Looty Bay has 28 robbery targets across four districts — from corner stores to the bank vault and the police armory. A clean job follows the same order every time. Skip a step and you meet the whole precinct.

  1. Scout as a Civilian. Find the alarm panel (usually at the back or side of the building), the cameras, the staff, the exits — and check where the cops are.
  2. Park facing your exit before you mask up. Hide the getaway car if you're on foot inside.
  3. Disable the alarm first, then mask up. If a camera sees you or the panel is untouched, the alarm trips in about 10–15 seconds and every cop sees it on the map, with your distance.
  4. Work fast, keep staff at gunpoint. Intimidated NPCs stay put; use lockpicks instead of breaking glass — quieter and it feeds less attention.
  5. Grab by value, not by volume. The single best item in the city is the Gold Bar ($52,000) from Looty Bay Bank. Drop grey junk for gold loot every time.
  6. Leave the city as soon as you're done — sell to the Fence on the way if your Notoriety streak is hot, then get out before the response arrives.

Target ladder — where to start, where to graduate

TierTargetsNotes
StarterConvenience stores, Rusty's Burgers, Loraine Hills mansionsBest first solo runs — close to a Fence, low response
MidJewellery stores, the Gas Station, Reef & Seasons hotelsGas Station has two hidden rooms — left and right, each with its own key
High valueArt Gallery (91 loot spots), Grand Hotel (55), Strip Club (48), Police Station (47)Bring a party of 3 and a plan; these light up the whole city

The bank vault, step by step

  1. Get a Drill from the Suspicious Door barter trader next to Lenny's Motel (barter recipe in Secrets).
  2. Park the getaway car, mask up, and drill the vault at Looty Bay Bank. Watch both staircases — post one player on each if you're a full party of 3.
  3. Prioritise Gold Bars. A Bank Vault ID Card opens the gold vault.
  4. Bank Money Bags carry a dye pack — don't sell them raw. Open them at your base's Cargo Workbench.
  5. Leave before the alarm countdown ends. A smaller bag you keep beats a bigger one you lose.
Never sell these Some loot is worth far more used than sold: a key can open a safe worth 200× its Fence price, a lottery ticket can land a huge payout (values in Secrets), and a jammer is needed to steal the Buletti supercar from the Grand Hotel. If you don't know what something does, store it — don't sell it.

09 Banking & laundering

Dirty cash is a liability. Laundering is how money becomes yours. It takes three steps, in this order:

  1. Open the account. Looty Bay Bank, as a Civilian, $5,000. No account = no laundering, no bribes, no clan.
  2. Get a plot and a house (next section). The Laundering Desk lives at your base.
  3. Load dirty cash into the Laundering Desk. Clean money lands in your bank account in portions — and the desk keeps working while you're offline. Banknote Counters and desk upgrades raise its capacity and speed.

Withdraw cash at an ATM or a bank employee when you need it — but remember, withdrawn cash can be stolen again. Before you own a desk, you have two worse options: launder small amounts through Lenny (he takes a cut) or by hand early on (you lose 50%). Both are bridges, not strategies.

Taxes are real: the settlement owner takes a cut of every resident's laundering and Black Market purchases, and the district's clan takes a share of the settlement owners' take. Owners collect their cut in person — and the cash they carry away can be robbed like anyone else's.

Your bank account is also your bribe fund — cop bribes are paid from it, in $10,000 steps up to $200,000.

10 House & base building

Your base is your respawn point, your storage, your garage, your bank vault and your business park in one. Getting a plot is the most important purchase of the wipe — plots go fast on a fresh server, so make it priority one.

How to get your first plot

  1. Research, then buy, a Land Plot Title. Titles live in Larry's Tree (the Documents branch of the research/Shipments tree — press H). Researching only unlocks the title; you still buy it separately on the Trade Laptop or from Lenny's Black Market. Since the Nov 4 update, Tier 1 land costs documents, not cash.
  2. Check the map for a free plot first. You can only rent in a settlement that already has an owner — you can't claim land in an unowned district. And the title's level must match the district's level. Don't buy an expensive title with nowhere to put it.
  3. Walk to the “For Rent” sign on a vacant plot and sign the rental with your title. You're now a Settlement Resident — which unlocks your base, new Shipments, the district Sales Center's better prices, and discounted contraband.
  4. Place your buildings from your inventory. Building is fully item-based: houses, fences, farms, garages, safes, racks and workbenches are items you buy or loot, then place. Your main building starts with a laptop, a first-aid kit and a few cabinets. You can move your whole base — everything in it — at any time.

Land Plot Title costs (community-reported)

TitleResearchPurchaseTotal
Level 1 Land Plot Title$50,000$100,000~$150,000
Level 2 Land Plot Title$200,000$800,000~$1,000,000
Level 3 Land Plot Title$1,000,000$2,000,000~$3,000,000
Level 1 Settlement Title (own a whole settlement)Research + purchase combined~$300,000

Level 2–3 district plots need special documents from the Black Market. Prices can vary by server and patch.

Build order — what to place first

  1. Storage — somewhere safe for the loot you're not selling.
  2. Laundering Desk (+ Banknote Counters) — turns dirty cash into money nobody can steal.
  3. Garage — unlocks owning your own car.
  4. Cargo Workbench — opening cargo yourself pays more than the Smuggler, and it's how you clean dye-packed Bank Money Bags.
  5. Security fuses on doors and gates — they slow raiders down and cost them more.
  6. Then: a lift for car modules, the Grow Room, the lab, a workshop and a warehouse. A helipad only matters if you find a helicopter.

Defending your base — and raiding others

No base is completely safe, but raiding is expensive by design. Attackers need Breach Decoders, which no shop sells — they're looted or bartered (1 Action Camera → 1 decoder at the Suspicious Door; 3 decoders + $10,000 → a higher-grade decoder). A decoder opens a building through its Security System for a short window; stronger Electronic Fuses make the hack take longer, and the owner can repair the system mid-raid and lock the attacker out. A full takeover needs an Eviction Right — bartered for 50 Raid Decoders — with every Security System hacked first.

Defense on a budget Kefir's own advice: fit defensive modules, set raid alerts for you and your allies — or simply look poor, so your base reads as a waste of rare breaching tools. Laundered bank money can't be raided at all, so keep wealth in the bank, not in boxes.

11 The weed farm & the chemical lab

Base businesses are the best steady earners in the game — Kefir “massively increased” their profits at launch. The Grow Room is the starter business; the lab is the bigger, smokier earner.

Grow Room (weed farm) — setup

PieceResearchPurchaseNotes
Grow Room$150,000$100,000Research in Larry's Tree, Production branch
Grow Table$30,000$40,000Each extra table $40,000; a room holds up to 6 tables × 6 bushes

That's about $320,000 for the room and your first table, on top of your plot. Buy both from the Trade Laptop at your base.

Finding Growing Bushes

Bushes are loot in Looty Bay. The most reliable reported spawns: the Gear Store, the Gun Shop on the south side of downtown, and Rusty's Burgers Café — with the S Club jewellery store office and pharmacy back rooms as less reliable options. Bushes count as cargo: draw a weapon and you'll drop the bush, and police can seize it. Solo players: grab one and drive straight home.

Grow, harvest, sell

  • Place a bush on an empty Grow Table. A clock shows while it grows; a tick means ready.
  • Harvesting takes a few seconds and yields 2–4 Harvest Bags — and the bush regrows at the same rarity.
  • Reported bag values: ~$4,000 Uncommon · ~$6,000 Epic · ~$8,000 Legendary.
  • Sell bags at a Fence or your district Sales Center, then launder the cash.
  • Table modules speed growth: Fan +12% · Water Pump +14% · UV Lamp +24% (higher tiers). Don't buy upgrades right before the wipe.

The chemical lab — the bigger earner

PieceResearchPurchase
Chemical Laboratory$160,000$110,000
Lab Table$10,000$15,000
Laboratory Scales$15,000$15,000

The chain: reagents go into the lab and become a concentrate → the freezer turns concentrate into crystals → you package them at the Lab Table with the Scales, then sell and launder like everything else.

Lab warning A working lab smokes — it advertises your base to everyone passing. Weigh the extra profit against the raid attention, and don't run it undefended.

12 Weapons, gear & vehicles

Weapons — there's no single best gun

Weapons come from city loot or the Black Market. Pick by the fight you're walking into:

ClassNamed gunsBest for
SMGsAP Scalar, JP-7Close fights, interiors
RiflesKL-545, RC 5.56, DRM-14Mid and long range
ShotgunsHarris 500, TAG-12KTight interiors, doorways
PistolsDP-9, Vulture 50Cheap backups — your first buy

There are deliberately no sniper rifles and damage falls off steeply at range — part of Kefir's design against wallhack-style cheating. Loot rarity runs grey → green → purple → gold, for gear, keys and cargo alike; purple and gold cargo is worth prioritising every run.

Tools of the trade

  • Lockpicks (Black Market): open doors, containers and car trunks silently. Picking another player's trunk — police cars included — gets you the trunk contents, not the car, and it counts as a crime that feeds your Notoriety.
  • Keys: every key's description says what it opens. Never sell them (see Secrets).
  • Breach Decoders: base-raiding only; looted or bartered, never shop-bought.
  • Drills & mini drills, glass cutters, USB tools: the heist toolkit — several come from barter at the Suspicious Door.

Vehicles

  • Rentals are free forever at Parking Terminals whenever you have no active vehicle.
  • To own a car you need a plot with a house or garage. Put the key in the key locker and the car appears in the garage. Owned cars survive your death, mods included. Modules fit the hood, trunk and underbody; a base lift lets you swap them yourself.
  • Helicopters can only be bought if your base is in the central Highlands district — or found in loot — and need a helipad.
  • Vehicles do not survive the weekly wipe and are confiscated if you change servers.

13 Playing as a cop

The other side of the mask. Cop pay is lower than crime, but the risk is lower too — and dying on duty costs you only department-issued gear.

  • Enlist at the Police Station in Looty Bay when a slot is open. Slots are capped (max 4 cops per city since the Nov 5 patch) and popular — expect a queue at peak times. Your personal belongings are stored for the shift and returned after.
  • You get free gear and a basic car from the state. On a fresh server, patrol cops carry pistols only for the first 30 minutes.
  • Income: a salary paid into your account, a percentage of confiscated loot, arrest rewards — plus bonuses for turning on the siren and demanding a surrender, and for answering backup calls.
  • Bribes are your call. A cornered criminal can offer up to $200,000 from their bank account. Accept and they walk with everything; refuse and take the bag.
  • Badges are your progression. Without one you get basic equipment only. Find badges in the city or buy them via the Trade Laptop after research; the sergeant's badge unlocks through Lenny. Badges are single-use and barter upward — 10 sergeant's badges → 1 lieutenant's, for example.
  • Cops respawn more slowly after each death — a deliberate balance lever. Criminals: an early-server fight against pistol cops is the fairest fight you'll get all week.
  • Cops can only shoot criminals. Civilians are off-limits.
Playing against cops Scout as a Civilian, disable alarms, use the ramps, hide the getaway car, and remember the bridges can be closed. If you're caught anyway: surrender (Q) and keep your gear — or bribe. Fighting a full response over a small bag is how wipes end early.

14 Power Pyramid, clans & districts

The desert outside Looty Bay is a shared map of ten districts made of hex settlements. Higher-level districts unlock better items and features — and a tax chain that flows uphill.

Hobo

Everyone starts here, living at Lenny's Motel.

Settlement Resident

Rent a plot, build a base, unlock the Sales Center and Shipments.

Settlement Owner

Buy a whole settlement (~$300,000 for Level 1), place your own base free, tax residents' laundering and Black Market buys. Nobody can seize your settlement before the wipe.

District Owner

Your clan controls a district and takes a cut of every settlement owner's taxes there — plus faster laundering, better at higher district levels.

Shadow Governor

Leader of the clan holding the central Highlands district. One per world. Best laundering rates on the map — and taxes every other clan.

The map

The central Highlands district is Level 3. A Level 2 ring — Rivertown, Fallrock and El Peso — surrounds it, and the outer districts are Level 1. Your Trade Laptop's tier equals the level of the district your plot sits in; with no plot, you're stuck at Tier I.

Clans and parties

  • Parties: up to 3. You can only invite on the global map or inside a settlement — not from some locations, and not a player in a clan conflict.
  • Clans: up to 100 players, on one server only. You need a bank account to create or join one, and you can switch clans during a wipe cycle.
  • Only clans can hold districts. Playing with friends on different servers? Pick the same server (called a “state”) at the selection screen before you build anything — switching later costs you everything on the old server (see The Wipe).
  • There's no direct cash transfer yet — players drop cash in a car trunk for a friend.

15 The weekly wipe — the Federal Raid

Every server wipes exactly seven days after it opened, in an event called the Federal Raid. There is no single global wipe day — your server's in-game Lifetime timer is the authority. The launch-day servers first wiped on Nov 11, 2026 at 5 PM UTC, and their next Raid falls Nov 25.

The Raid takes

  • All cash — carried, stashed at your base, and laundered bank money
  • Plots, bases and real estate
  • Weapons, gear, vehicles and contraband
  • Unlocked research / tech-tree items

You keep

  • Cosmetics and B-Coins
  • Your character's appearance and name
  • Tutorial progress and settings
  • Jail Time — and since the Nov 17 update, Battle Pass points and region-change progress carry over too

Everything the Feds confiscate is converted into Jail Time and Authority — the richer you were, the longer your sentence, and that's a badge of honour: accumulated Jail Time unlocks tattoos, Authority perks and some Shipments items. Rich players pile up more of it. The wipe isn't the end of your progress; it's the score screen.

Wipe calculator — when does your server reset?


Pick the day your server opened and I'll work out its Federal Raid.

Fresh servers open daily — EU 5 PM UTC, East US 8 PM ET — and each wipes 7 days after it opens, so wipe times roll through the day rather than landing all at once.

End-of-wipe strategy

  • Spend, don't save. Banked money dies in the Raid exactly like carried cash. Convert late-week cash into Jail Time value: big purchases, big labs, big risks.
  • Don't buy base upgrades in the last day or two — they won't pay for themselves before the reset.
  • Take the fights you'd normally avoid. Gear you lose on day 7 was being confiscated anyway.
  • Changing servers (“states”): pick from the state-selection list before entering — or, if you're already in, open the world map → prison → Surrender to Feds, then switch. Switching confiscates everything you own in the old state and removes you from your clan; tattoos, B-Coins, cosmetics (and now progress/Battle Pass points) are kept. Re-send party invites afterwards.

16 Cheats, hacks & secrets — the straight truth

You asked for cheats, hacks and secrets, so here's all three — including the part the cheat sellers won't tell you.

The real “cheats”: secrets the game doesn't explain

  • Solo is a cheat code in disguise. Solo players start at Notoriety 4 (+35% at the Fence) while a duo starts at 2. Same loot, a third more money — if you can survive the run.
  • The Civilian Fence run. Haul at risk? Exit to the global map and re-enter as a Civilian to reach the Fence. Civilians keep gear and bag even when killed.
  • Never sell a key. The Fence pays ~$500 for a key; the safe or room it opens pays $100,000–$150,000. The Gas Station alone hides two rooms, each with its own key.
  • Lottery tickets are a goldmine. Five variants hide in safes and cabinets: Common $1 · Uncommon $40 · Epic $10,000 · Legendary $250,000 · Exotic $1,000,000 at Fence level 1 — and at level 5 the bonuses push the Legendary to $375,000 and the Exotic to $1,500,000. Check every safe.
  • Charge-up items multiply your heists. An Action Camera bought for $15,000 sells filled for $50,000+; a USB Hacking Tool turns $50,000 into $200,000. Sell a full set together at Notoriety 5 for the +50% bonus.
  • The Suspicious Door is a barter goldmine. The trader next to Lenny's Motel swaps: 3 Code Tablets → a Glass Cutter; an Epic Action Camera + 2 Legendary USB Hacking Tools + $50,000 → a Drill (your bank-vault key); 1 Action Camera → a Breach Decoder for raids.
  • Dye-packed Bank Money Bags look like a trap — they're a bonus. Open them at your Cargo Workbench instead of selling them raw.
  • The Buletti heist. The Grand Hotel's Buletti supercar needs a jammer to steal — one of the items new players sell by accident. The Fabergé Egg is the other marquee steal. Store first, sell never (until you know).
  • Collections pay stupid money late. A basic Collection Crate delivers $50,000; Rare and Unique crates reach $150,000 and $500,000. There are 34 collections — the Collection Table ($5,000 research / $15,000 buy) turns “junk” loot runs into a second income.
  • Lenny's stash is a free vault. $150,000, unstealable, no plot needed. Early game, it's your bank until the Laundering Desk exists.
  • Fresh-server cops are pistol-only for 30 minutes, and cop respawns get slower with every death. The first hour of a new server is the softest the city will ever be.
  • Roulette at the Bar uses in-game money only — and no, there is no published strategy that beats it. It's flavour, not income.

“Hacks” — read this before you touch one

Ban warning — this is the whole section, in one paragraph Kefir banned over 20,000 accounts for cheating by Nov 13, 2026 — up from 4,000+ two days earlier — and says detection is getting faster. The game runs Easy Anti-Cheat plus server-side checks that already block speed hacks, wall phasing, flying/teleporting, god mode and inventory snooping. Kefir's official Ban Policy (Nov 17) runs from 24 hours to 5 years depending on severity, and Kefir may not even tell you the specific grounds. Appeals go through Kefir support. An aimbot or ESP from a cheat site is the fastest known way to lose a free account — permanently.
  • The cheat sites are the real scam. The “ROB RUN aimbot / ESP / FOV changer” pages flooding search results sell subscriptions to software that gets detected in waves — and the free downloads in that scene are a classic malware delivery route. You risk your Steam account and your PC, not just a game ban.
  • There is no mobile version to hack. Every “ROB RUN APK,” “ROB RUN Mobile” download and install-video funnel (the ones sending you to third-party “app center” sites) is fake — Kefir has no Android or iOS build. Those downloads are not the game.
  • Real-money trading is banned too. Kefir's community rules prohibit trading in-game currency for real money; the “dirty cash delivered to your server” ads are a ban risk and a payment scam in one package.
  • What actually works instead: everything in the secrets list above is legal, repeatable, and — stacked together (solo Notoriety + charged items + Workbench cargo + a farm) — out-earns what a banned account makes. Which is zero.

Spotted a cheater? Report them properly

  1. Use the Report button on the death screen (made more prominent in the Nov 17 update), or report via the official Discord / help centre.
  2. Copy your UID (Esc → under your character name), and note the server/region and the time in UTC.
  3. Attach a clip if you have one. Reports with evidence are the ones that land.

17 Error codes & fixes

From Kefir's help centre. Most fixes come down to one move: fully restart the game and Steam, then verify the game files (Steam → Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity).

CodeMeaningFix
E-0101 / E-0110Can't reach the serverCheck your connection; check server status first (below)
E-0102Data blockedPublic Wi-Fi, a proxy, or antivirus HTTPS scanning is interfering — switch network / whitelist the game
E-0301 / E-0302Outdated versionRestart Steam and update
E-0303 / E-0304Corrupted dataWait 10–15 minutes, then verify game files
E-0401Steam authentication failureConfirm Steam is in online mode and you're on the right account
E-0501 / E-0502Easy Anti-Cheat not runningRestart; let EAC start with the game, don't block it
E-0601No keyboard and mouse detectedConnect physical devices; don't launch over Remote Desktop / cloud streaming

“Waiting for status information” / stuck loading?

It means the game is waiting on the server list or a server response. First check whether the servers are actually up — launch week brought repeated DDoS attacks, multi-hour outages and progress rollbacks, and a planned restart takes about 30 minutes. If player counts look normal and there's no outage post: fully restart the game and Steam (Kefir says a restart picks up their new server configuration), verify files, and update your graphics driver. If counts are near zero, it's the servers — wait it out.

18 FAQ

Is ROB RUN free? Is it pay to win?

Yes, free on Steam, and no — Kefir sells only cosmetics (B-Coins) with zero gameplay advantage, and says the game stays free after Early Access. No paid DLC, editions or subscription.

Is ROB RUN on PS5, Xbox, mobile or Mac?

No. Windows PC via Steam is the only official way to play. No console, Android, iOS, Mac or Linux version exists or has been announced — and any “ROB RUN APK” is not Kefir's game.

Is ROB RUN the same as Roblox?

No — different game, different company, nothing shared but three letters. ROB RUN is Kefir's M-rated crime sandbox about robbing a city run by real players.

How do I play with friends?

Parties hold up to 3 players; clans up to 100. Pick the same server at the state-selection screen before anyone builds anything. Invites only work on the global map or inside a settlement. If a friend is on another server, one of you has to switch via the prison (world map → prison → Surrender to Feds) — and switching confiscates everything owned on the old server.

How do I get a house?

Research and buy a Land Plot Title (Larry's Tree → Trade Laptop, or Lenny's Black Market), find a vacant plot in a player-owned settlement whose level matches your title, sign at the “For Rent” sign, then place your house and buildings from your inventory. Full walkthrough in the Base section.

How do I launder money?

Open a bank account at Looty Bay Bank as a Civilian ($5,000), get a plot, place a Laundering Desk at your base, and load dirty cash into it. Clean money lands in your account and can't be stolen — until the wipe. See Banking & Laundering.

What happens when I get caught?

Surrender (Q) and cops take only your bag — equipped gear stays. Bribe from your bank account (up to $200,000) and you might walk with everything. Die masked and you lose gear and bag; die as a Civilian in the city and you lose nothing.

What survives the weekly wipe?

Cosmetics, B-Coins, your name and appearance, tutorial progress, settings, accumulated Jail Time — and, since Nov 17, Battle Pass points and region-change progress. Cash, bases, weapons and vehicles do not survive.

Are there cheat codes or promo codes?

There are no official cheat codes or promo codes in ROB RUN. The “cheats” that exist are the game's own hidden systems — Notoriety stacking, charge-up items, barter recipes and hidden rooms — all covered in the Secrets section. Third-party hack tools get accounts banned (24 hours to 5 years).
